items.excerpt: Snap's SPECS see-through AR glasses are officially up for pre-order at $2,195 with fall 2026 delivery: dual Snapdragon processors, RGB and infrared cameras and computer-vision sensors feed real-time spatial awareness so the built-in AI understands what you're looking at — a very different bet on AR's future than Apple Vision Pro.

Meta is putting Conversation Focus — the smart glasses' audio-amplification feature that runs entirely on-device using beamforming mics and onboard processing — behind its $20/month Meta One Premium tier, capping free users at 3 hours a month and premium users at 15, despite no cloud costs to justify the limits.

Review of the HP OmniBook Ultra 14 (2026), a Copilot+ PC built on Qualcomm's Snapdragon X2 Elite: potent NPU-backed Arm performance and standout battery endurance make it one of the stronger AI laptops of the year, at a premium price.

MemoMind One, the first smart glasses from XGIMI's new AI hardware brand, blasted past $500K on Kickstarter: dual green micro-LED displays, an on-device AI assistant, 26-language real-time translation and an optional Memo+ subscription that builds searchable long-term memory of meetings and conversations, from $400.

HMD quietly launched four new Nokia feature phones (200/210/215/235 4G) with dedicated AI assistant buttons: the S30+ handsets ship with the voice-controlled Sikey AI assistant for calls, reminders and basic queries — free for the first 180 days, then locked behind a subscription.

Hands-on with Gemini Live running on Android Auto during a drive across Romania: the conversational AI is brilliant for multi-language chat and staying alert at the wheel, but phone incompatibilities, mandatory screen taps to end sessions and total dropouts when Maps navigation kicks in leave it feeling very broken.

Rogbid's $119.99 VisionPro smart glasses launch with a 13 MP Sony camera, up to 12 hours of battery and a dual-chip AI architecture handling real-time object and landmark recognition, printed-text translation, live multilingual conversation translation and a voice assistant — undercutting Meta's glasses at a fraction of the price.

Analysis of how the AI/AR glasses hardware race is accelerating beyond expectations — and it's not just Google and Xreal's Aura glasses pushing the boundaries, as waveguide displays and on-device AI assistants converge across the category.

Android chief Sameer Samat details Android Halo and how Gemini is being wired into hardware — including using cars' front-facing cameras so drivers can ask the AI about what's happening in front of the vehicle — as on-device Gemini spreads across Android devices.

48 hours with XGIMI's MemoMind One XR glasses, a waveguide-display AI wearable: slow AI responses, no camera and disappointing audio leave the reviewer questioning why you'd pick them in an increasingly crowded sea of AI smart glasses.

Review of Meta's prescription-ready Ray-Ban Meta Optics smart glasses: improved fit, a new action button and enhanced Meta AI powered by the Muse Spark model, weighed against privacy concerns and a $700+ price when configured with custom lenses.

Hands-on with Meta's first self-branded AI glasses lineup — the Meta Adventurer, Meta Fury and Meta Glasses by Kylie (Jenner) — $299 smart glasses that shed the Ray-Ban branding while keeping the Gen 2 hardware and debuting the Muse Spark AI companion app.

Google is rolling out a wave of Gemini for Home updates to its smart speakers and cameras, sharpening voice-assistant responses and camera intelligence ahead of the Gemini-first Google Home Speaker's arrival.
